title: About the Hardrock Hundred Mile Endurance Run
claims: The run is 101.8 miles with 33,441 feet of climb and 33,441 feet of descent, 66,882 feet of total elevation change, at an average elevation of over 11,000 feet.
The course is a loop on 4WD roads, dirt trails and cross country in the San Juan Range.
The 2026 run is clockwise and the 2027 run will be counter-clockwise; the direction reverses each year.
The course crosses thirteen major passes in the 12,000-13,000 ft range and goes above 12,000 feet thirteen times; the high point is Handies Peak at 14,048 feet.
The run has been held in early July each year since 1992, except 1995, 2002, 2019 and 2020.
The finish requires kissing the Hardrock, a ram's head painted on a block of mining debris.
The cut-off time is 48 hours; the average finishing time is 39:52:11; the fastest performances are Ludovic Pommeret 21:11 in 2026 and Katie Schide 25:50 in 2025.
The run starts at 6am, so runners finishing in over 40 hours see the sun set twice.
The course is described as a graduate-level challenge requiring mountaineering, wilderness survival and wilderness navigation skills.
